title: Height-Balanced Directory Trees for Re-Runnable HPC Benchmark Campaigns in Kotlin
topic: Thinflow: Organizing HPC Benchmarking Campaigns as Rerunnable Directory Trees
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: High-performance computing (HPC) benchmarking campaigns routinely generate nested directory trees that encode experiment metadata and execution scripts. Managing these trees as immutable, rerunnable structures enables reproducibility and efficient incremental execution. We present AetherFlow, a Kotlin-based framework that models benchmark campaigns as height-balanced directory trees, supporting atomic insertion, lookup, and deep-clone rerun operations. AetherFlow preserves a strict height-balance invariant and key-ordered property, guaranteeing $O(\log N)$ search and insertion complexity. Formal proofs establish that the tree remains balanced after each mutation. Static abstract syntax tree (AST) inspection confirms that the implementation comprises 124 source lines and a single function block, yielding an auxiliary memory bound of $O(N)$. No empirical runtime measurements are reported; all claims are supported by static analysis and formal reasoning. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/kotlin-systems-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261122_140132_thinflow__organizing_hpc_bench}
